To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the natural vitamin nicotinamide-riboside (NR) increases NAD(+/) and activates SIRTs 1 and 3 in vivo, leading to enhanced oxidative metabolism, improved insulin sensitivity, and protection against diet-induced metabolic disorders.

nicotinamide-riboside supplementation in mice increases mitochondrial NAD(+) and SIRT3 levels, resulting in enhanced oxidative metabolism, and protection against high fat diet induced metabolic abnormalities.
the NAD(+)precursor nicotinamide-riboside enhances oxidative-metabolism and protects against highfat diet-induced obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic approaches to treat metabolic diseases, such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.
the identification of a novel NAD(+) supplement that could be used in the treatment of metabolic and age-related diseases.
the identification and characterization of new compounds with the ability to activate SIRT1 and improve mitochondrial function and metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NR is a natural vitamin that is able to increase the NAD+ levels in cells, and this increase in NAD+ levels is associated with activation of SIRT enzymes, increased energy expenditure and improved metabolic health.

the natural vitamin precursor nicotinamic riboside (vitamin B3), when supplemented, increases NAD+ levels and activates Sirtuin 1 and 3, which in turn increases mitochondrial function and oxidative metabolism.

NR is a NAD(+) biosynthetic precursor that increases the levels of NAD(+) in cells and tissues and activates SIRTs, resulting in enhanced mitochondrial function and protection against high fat diet-induced obesity and metabolic disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NR supplementation increases mitochondrial function and protects against metabolic disease.
NR supplementation is a promising nutritional approach for metabolic disorders associated with mitochondrial dysfunction.

the NAD(+) precursors, nicotinamide and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotin- amide riboside (NAD(+)-ribose) are effective in raising NAD(+) and sirtuin activity in cells, and that this can be achieved by oral administration in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the natural compound nicotinamide-riboside (NR) can be used as a dietary supplement to increase NAD levels and SIRT activity, and to protect against metabolic disorders.

the NAD(+) biosynthetic precursor nicotinamic riboside (or NR) can increase the levels of the coenzyme NAD(+) and, consequently, activate the NAD(+)-consuming enzymes sirtuins, leading to increased oxidative metabolism.
NAD(+) precursors such as nicotinamide mononucleotide and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide riboside (NAD+) can enhance mitochondrial function and improve metabolic health.
